habitat: Mature miombo, and also Baikiaea and tall mopane woodland. Breeding birds use extensive, well-developed woodland. In winter, non-breeding birds may use smaller stands, including riparian acacia. It feeds in the canopy and is usually alone or in pairs.
summary: An uncommon woodland cuckooshrike. Newman has no page for it. The SABAP1 text describes habitat and movements, not plumage: it is a canopy feeder of tall broad-leaved woodland, overlooked because it is inconspicuous, and in the old Transvaal it is treated as resident with local movements and is most often recorded in winter. Wikipedia adds dry forest and dry savanna, and an insect diet. No plumage description was found in those sources, so the marks were left empty.

similar.note: Grey Cuckooshrike is the forest bird and is grey all over. SABAP1 says the two are ecologically separated. This species uses tall woodland.

research.note: Newman has no species page. Habitat and the resident status come from SABAP1, which says Transvaal birds are resident with local winter movements and are most often recorded in winter. All twelve months are listed because that text does not treat it as absent in summer. Plumage and the call were not described in the sources consulted, so no colour marks were stored. The photograph is from Kruger and the caption does not turn its colours into field marks. The call file is grade A from Zambia. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.
